prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: one high-fidelity, production-realistic desktop web screenshot comp for a personal technical blog article page
Canvas: exactly 1440 × 900 pixels, landscape. Show the first viewport only, edge to edge, with no browser chrome and no device frame.

Input images:
- Image 1 is the current live Vartifact article page. Use it as the exact product identity, content hierarchy, warm editorial tone, and restraint reference. Preserve its real article identity, but redesign the layout as specified below. Do not copy its old Writing/About/Contact navigation.
- Image 2 is the exact article cover photograph. Use this real canal photograph unchanged in subject and color, cropped cinematically inside the cover strip. Do not invent or replace the photo.

Primary request:
Create the Vartifact article-page redesign in the direction “Film Leader.” It must look like a realistic, shippable screenshot of a reading website, not an abstract moodboard, poster, or concept art. The visual system is “Contact Sheet Reading Room”: restrained 35mm film leader and editorial contact strip on warm proof paper. The film motif supports navigation and chronology but stays quiet enough that prose is the main reading experience.

Exact first-viewport structure:
1. A slim 72px header on proof paper. “Vartifact” at left. At right, exactly “READ”, “NOTES”, and “ABOUT” as small Huninn-like sans navigation. READ is active with a precise oxide-red underline or registration tick. One flat hairline rule spans below the header.
2. Below, a generous editorial hero occupying roughly the next 430px. Use a three-part horizontal composition: a very narrow vertical numbered film rail at far left of the content area; an authored title block beside it; and a wide cinematic cover strip on the right.
3. The film rail is near-black, narrow and functional, with small sprocket perforations and restrained frame numbers such as “01”, “02”, “03”. Keep it narrow: it must not compete with the title.
4. The title block uses an Iansui-like Traditional Chinese serif/handwritten serif voice. Set the exact title “初次使用 Astro.js” large but not oversized. Directly below, set the exact dek “為什麼使用 Astro.js 來打造部落格”. Add a calm byline and date/meta row using the exact strings “Michael Tsai”, “2025 年 2 月 2 日”, “1 MIN READ”, and “0 VIEWS”. Use small Huninn-like sans labels with tabular numerals.
5. The cover is a low, wide cinematic strip, not a giant hero image. Use Image 2 as the exact photo, held by a square near-black film edge with a slim caption rail, tiny crop/registration marks, and one small oxide-red mark. No rounded image.
6. Under the hero, transition through one thin rule into a centered article reading column about 65 characters wide. Make the reading column start high enough that the first two short paragraphs of Traditional Chinese article prose are visibly readable in this 900px viewport. The prose is Iansui-like serif, near-black, approximately 18px with open line height. Include a modest first paragraph about selecting Astro.js for a content-focused blog, with no invented claims, promotions, or new product features.
7. Allow generous proof-paper margins and disciplined alignment. Use square frames, flat hairlines, tiny crop marks, and restrained frame numbering. Do not place the body prose in a card.

Palette and materials:
- Proof paper background #ebe3d8
- Near-black text #1f1e1d
- Oxide red signal #a33f29 used only for active/selected/progress marks
- Film black #1c1a1a
- Very subtle real paper grain is allowed, but keep the surface flat and readable.

Typography:
- Iansui-like serif for the authored title, dek, and article body.
- Huninn-like friendly sans for navigation, metadata, labels, and film numbers.
- Only these two type voices. Keep Traditional Chinese glyphs accurate and fully legible.

Text, verbatim:
“Vartifact”
“READ”
“NOTES”
“ABOUT”
“初次使用 Astro.js”
“為什麼使用 Astro.js 來打造部落格”
“Michael Tsai”
“2025 年 2 月 2 日”
“1 MIN READ”
“0 VIEWS”

Constraints:
- Preserve every required string exactly with correct capitalization and Traditional Chinese characters.
- Keep the opening article text visible in the first viewport.
- Use the real cover image from Image 2.
- Prioritize readable hierarchy and realistic spacing over decorative film effects.
- Flat UI: no gradients, no glass, no blur effects, no generic cards, no rounded containers, no glossy 3D, no heavy shadows.
- No new logo, no new brand name, no new navigation items, no badges, no dashboard layout, no commercial claims, no watermark.
- Exactly one desktop page comp.
